summary: Both claims the author asked me to verify HOLD, re-run in a sandbox repo with a real HEAD: gate 1 is green on a clean tree and green on the real staged M0.76 row, red at 'row M0.99 is 4224 chars, cap 4000'; gate 2 is green on a clean tree, red on the exact comment, and green on a comment that merely names another test. The median 1306 / p90 5127 figures in the gate header are exact. Beyond those checks, four findings. (1) Neither gate has a test, against a repo convention where 15 of 22 gates do and the nearest sibling check-session-load.sh has BacklogBoundsTest, whose own Javadoc says a bound with no counter-case is indistinguishable from a gate that refuses everything: with ARCHIVE_ROW_CAP defaulted to 999999999 and PATTERN set to a never-matching literal, ./gradlew -p buildSrc test --rerun-tasks is BUILD SUCCESSFUL. (2) Gate 1 recognises rows by the literal prefix '+| M', so six reachable row shapes -- two spaces after the pipe, no space, a markdown-legal leading space, a non-M id, a lowercase id, a blank first cell -- carry a 4224-char row past it while it prints 'ok 0 archive row(s) added, each within 4000 chars'; the sibling gate already solved this with a tolerant regex. (3) Neither gate honours or prints GATE_SCOPE, so under CI's GATE_SCOPE=full both print an unqualified ok over a tree that contains an oversized row and an inventory comment -- and the M0.77 row staged in this same commit says the gate finds those files 'in full mode', which returns ok/0. (4) Gate 2's regex false-positives on seven legitimate comment shapes including its own prescribed remedy. Minors: 11 existing instances of the exact target shape are invisible because the phrase wraps across a line; the cap is locale-dependent; both gates fail open on an unresolvable CHECK_RANGE; the '~19 files' figure is measurably 31.

findings.title: Neither gate has a test, so nothing in the tree pins the discrimination the gate exists to provide
findings.detail: The gates ARE the deliverable here, and they are the thing that must fail when the guarded property is violated. The repository's own convention is that a gate is pinned by a buildSrc JUnit test that mutates it: 15 of the 22 check-*.sh have at least one test file naming them (check-module.sh 8, check-reviewed.sh 3, check-session-load.sh 2). The nearest sibling -- check-session-load.sh, from which this cap idea is taken -- has BacklogBoundsTest.java, whose Javadoc states the standard directly: 'each test carries its own negative control, because a bound with no counter-case is indistinguishable from a gate that refuses everything'. review.md rule harness-exempt states the same thing as the replacement for a reviewer on gate code: 'a gate is verified by mutating it and watching a test fail'. There is no test to fail. The proof offered instead is a manual run recorded in a backlog row, which is precisely the 'resolution I promise to keep' the task says it is replacing with a predicate over the tree.
findings.mutation_that_survives: In scripts/check-archive-row-size.sh:17 change the default to ARCHIVE_ROW_CAP:=999999999, and in scripts/check-test-inventory-claims.sh:28 set PATTERN='zzzz-this-can-never-match-zzzz'. Both gates now accept everything. MEASURED in my own review tree: `./gradlew -p buildSrc test --rerun-tasks` -> BUILD SUCCESSFUL, 13 tasks executed. Every other finding below is a live regression that this same absence would let land silently tomorrow.
findings.remedy: An ArchiveRowSizeTest and a TestInventoryClaimsTest in buildSrc, in the shape of BacklogBoundsTest: a scratch repo, a positive control (an oversized row / the target comment -> exit 1) and a negative control (a normal row / a comment naming another test -> exit 0).
findings.failure_scenario: A future edit neuters either gate and nothing objects. Concretely: someone raises ARCHIVE_ROW_CAP or narrows PATTERN 'to reduce noise', the pre-commit run stays green, CI stays green, and the two failure modes this task exists to prevent are unguarded again -- with AGENTS.md still listing both gates as enforcing them. Measured: with the cap at 999999999 and PATTERN set to a never-matching literal, ./gradlew -p buildSrc test --rerun-tasks is BUILD SUCCESSFUL.

findings.title: The row recogniser is the literal prefix '+| M'; six reachable row shapes are skipped SILENTLY while the success line claims 0 rows were added
findings.detail: MEASURED in a sandbox repo with a real HEAD. Each of these stages a 4224-char archive row and the gate exits 0 printing 'ok 0 archive row(s) added, each within 4000 chars': '|  M0.99 | ...' (two spaces, the shape any table prettifier produces), '|M0.99 | ...' (no space), ' | M0.99 | ...' (one leading space, legal markdown), '| R1 | ...' (a non-M id), '| m0.99 | ...' (lowercase), '|  | M0.99 ... |' (blank first cell). The gate does not merely miss them -- `count` is only incremented for rows it recognises, so its success message affirmatively reports that nothing oversized was added. That is the exact defect class the review lens names: a gate reporting success while checking nothing. The threat model the task states is the author's own future self under pressure ('nine rounds of evidence say my intentions do not hold under pressure'), and a one-character change to the row's leading whitespace defeats it. The sibling gate for the same file family already solves this at scripts/check-session-load.sh:~118 with ROW = re.compile(r'^\|\s*(M-?\d+\.\d+[a-z]?)\s*\|').
findings.mutation_that_survives: No production mutation is needed -- the gate already fails to judge a 4224-char row under any of the six shapes above. Conversely, deleting lines 30-33 entirely (judging every '+|' line) would make the gate STRICTER, and nothing in the tree would notice either way.
findings.remedy: Match '^\+\|\s*([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9.-]*)\s*\|' as the sibling does, and fail (or at minimum warn) on a '+|' line whose first cell cannot be parsed as an id, rather than silently continuing while counting 0.
findings.failure_scenario: An author adds a 4224-char essay row to backlog-done.md with two spaces after the leading pipe (the shape a markdown table formatter produces), or as a non-M id. check-archive-row-size prints 'ok 0 archive row(s) added, each within 4000 chars' and exits 0. The commit lands, the archive grows an essay row, and the gate's output says it checked and found nothing.

findings.title: Neither gate honours or prints GATE_SCOPE, so under CI's GATE_SCOPE=full both print an unqualified ok over a tree that violates them
findings.detail: scripts/lib.sh states the contract: 'Every gate PRINTS its mode. A delta pass is a weaker statement than a full pass and must not read like one -- non-negotiable 4.' Neither new gate calls scoped_files or scope_note; GATE_SCOPE is a complete no-op in both. MEASURED, sandbox with a committed 4224-char row and a committed inventory comment: `GATE_SCOPE=full scripts/check-archive-row-size.sh` -> 'ok 0 archive row(s) added, each within 4000 chars', exit 0; `GATE_SCOPE=full scripts/check-test-inventory-claims.sh` -> 'ok 0 added comment line(s) in tests, none an assertion inventory', exit 0. MEASURED on the real repository: `GATE_SCOPE=full scripts/check-test-inventory-claims.sh` prints ok while 31 files carry the target shape. The consequence is concrete and is staged in this very commit: the M0.77 row at docs/internal/product/backlog.md:67 says the gate 'finds [these] in full mode'. There is no full mode. A session picking up M0.77 runs GATE_SCOPE=full, sees ok, and closes the row as already done. .github/workflows/ci.yml:90-96 also now carries a stale comment claiming CHECK_RANGE 'drives NOTHING that runs here' -- these two gates are new CHECK_RANGE consumers and neither is in the SKIP list.
findings.mutation_that_survives: Delete the entire `if [ -n "${CHECK_RANGE:-}" ]` branch from either gate and hardcode the --cached path. The CI nightly (schedule) run, which is the run whose stated purpose is catching what a delta cannot, would keep printing ok -- a fresh checkout has nothing staged -- and no test or gate in the tree would fail.
findings.remedy: Either print the mode explicitly (e.g. append scope_note or a literal '(added lines only -- NOT a full-tree statement)') so the ok line cannot be read as a full pass, or implement a full mode. Whichever is chosen, correct the 'in full mode' claim in the M0.77 row and the now-false CHECK_RANGE comment in ci.yml.
findings.failure_scenario: The nightly CI run, whose stated purpose is to catch what a delta cannot, runs GATE_SCOPE=full and prints 'ok 0 added comment line(s) in tests, none an assertion inventory' while 31 files in the tree carry the shape. Worse and already staged: a session picks up M0.77, whose row says the gate finds these files 'in full mode', runs GATE_SCOPE=full, sees ok/0, and closes the row as already done -- leaving 31 files of the exact prose M0.77 exists to remove.

findings.title: The regex flags seven legitimate comment shapes, including the remedy the gate itself prescribes and testing.md's own vocabulary
findings.detail: MEASURED, each staged as a single added comment line in a *Test.java and each turning the gate RED: (a) '// the only test double here is a fake, never a mock.' -- testing.md rule 18's own words; (b) '// the only assertion in THIS test that touches the clock.' -- self-referential, and the gate's charter is explicitly about assertions ELSEWHERE; (c) '// the only test in this class that needs Docker; tagged T4.'; (d) '// the only absolute path in the fixture; the rest are relative.' -- the alternation 'the only (test|assertion|absolute)' takes a bare 'absolute' and so matches 'the only absolute path', 'the only absolute requirement', anything; (e) '// every assertion here states a property, never a count.' -- a comment written to COMPLY with this gate is rejected by it, and the failure message tells the author to 'state the PROPERTY instead'; (f) '// the only assertion the SPI makes is that offsets are monotonic.' -- a statement about production, not about tests; (g) '// the request carries no other assertion of identity.'. Separately, the comment detector at 43-46 treats any line containing an asterisk as a comment, so `int n = a * b; String s = "the only assertion";` is flagged as a comment (measured). The script header names the failure mode this creates -- 'a gate that fails CI on legacy is a gate someone turns off' -- and a gate that rejects its own remedy sentence reaches that state without any legacy involved.
findings.mutation_that_survives: Replace the whole alternation with the single term 'the only absolute'. Five of the seven false positives above still fire, the gate still catches nothing it should, and nothing in the tree fails.
findings.remedy: Drop the bare 'absolute' alternative (require 'the only absolute (count|assertion)'), scope 'the only test/assertion' to forms that reference elsewhere, and detect comments by a leading '//', '*' or '/*' after whitespace rather than by 'contains an asterisk anywhere'.
findings.failure_scenario: An author writes '// the only test double here is a fake, never a mock' (testing.md rule 18's own wording), or the remedy the gate's failure message demands -- '// every assertion here states a property, never a count'. The commit is refused. Having no way to satisfy a gate that rejects its own prescribed fix, they SKIP=check-test-inventory-claims, and the gate stops running for everything else in that commit too.

findings.title: The matcher is line-scoped; 11 existing instances of the exact target shape are invisible because the phrase wraps at 80 columns
findings.detail: MEASURED on the real tree by joining consecutive comment lines before matching: 11 live sentences of exactly the shape the gate targets straddle a line break and are therefore unreachable by it. Verified by eye, e.g. format/src/test/java/binjava/format/LeaseTest.java:281 '...survived every / other test...', sequencer/src/test/java/binjava/sequencer/CommitLogTest.java:307 '...because every other / assertion here is...', sequencer/src/test/java/binjava/sequencer/FaultInjectingStoreStreamsTest.java:98 '...survived every other / test...'. Against 48 line-level hits in the same corpus that is a ~19% miss rate caused by nothing more adversarial than the project's own hard-wrap style. Recorded as minor because the gate is avowedly a shape-matcher on added lines and still catches four in five; it is not a false green about something it claims to have examined.
findings.mutation_that_survives: Write the target sentence and let the editor wrap it: '// every other' / '// test here is blind to it.' passes (measured). Also passing (measured): a block comment whose body line has no leading star; 'none of the other tests catch this'; 'this is the sole assertion pinning the bound'; 'survived all 294 unit tests'; 'all 294 tests passed with the mutation in place'; 'no test other than this one constrains it'; 'every other case in this file is blind to it'.
findings.remedy: Join a run of consecutive added comment lines, strip the leaders, and match the joined text -- about eight lines of the same shell/python already in the tree.
findings.failure_scenario: An author writes exactly the sentence the gate targets, the editor wraps it at 80 columns -- '// ...survived every other' / '// test in this file' -- and the gate passes. That is not hypothetical: 11 sentences of precisely that shape are already in the tree and unreachable by the gate for this reason alone, so the shape the task was written to stop is already landing in its most common form.

findings.title: The cap is locale-dependent: ${#line} counts characters under a UTF-8 locale and bytes under LC_ALL=C, so the same row gets opposite verdicts
findings.detail: MEASURED on one staged row built from 1300 repetitions of the warning emoji: LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 -> 'ok 1 archive row(s) added, each within 4000 chars', exit 0; LC_ALL=C -> 'FAIL row M0.98 is 9126 chars, cap 4000', exit 1. The archive's prose is emoji- and em-dash-dense, so the char/byte gap is real rather than theoretical (the staged M0.76 row is 1385 chars / 1403 bytes). C locale is the stricter direction, so this cannot produce a false pass against the char cap, but it can fail in a CI container on a row that passed on the author's machine -- and the message says 'chars' while reporting bytes. The sibling check-session-load.sh has the mirror-image inconsistency (it measures characters and calls them bytes), so picking one unit and stating it would settle both.
findings.mutation_that_survives: Change line 35 to n=$(printf '%s' "$line" | wc -c) -- switching the unit outright. Nothing in the tree fails, and the gate's behaviour on emoji-dense rows changes silently.
findings.remedy: Pin the unit (LC_ALL=C for bytes, or measure in python as the sibling does) and say which one the message reports.
findings.failure_scenario: CI runs in a container defaulting to LC_ALL=C or POSIX. A row of 3,910 characters that passed on the author's machine is reported as '9126 chars, cap 4000' and CI goes red on a commit that passed pre-commit -- a divergence between local and CI verdicts on identical bytes, which is the shape of gate that gets disabled.

findings.title: Both gates fail OPEN on an unresolvable CHECK_RANGE, contradicting the principle ci.yml states for exactly this case
findings.detail: MEASURED: CHECK_RANGE=deadbeefdeadbeef -> both gates print ok and exit 0 over a tree containing a 4224-char row and an inventory comment. The `2>/dev/null` plus `|| true` swallows git's failure and yields an empty diff, which reads as 'nothing was added'. .github/workflows/ci.yml:78-88 goes to considerable length to state the opposite rule -- 'fail when a range cannot be determined, rather than defaulting to a value that silently means check nothing' -- and resolves the range itself, so this is unreachable through today's CI wiring. It is a latent vacuous pass for any other caller.
findings.mutation_that_survives: Set CHECK_RANGE to any string that is not a valid rev. Both gates report success having examined nothing, and no test notices.
findings.remedy: Drop `|| true`, keep stderr, and fail when the range does not resolve.
findings.failure_scenario: Any caller that sets CHECK_RANGE to a ref this checkout does not have -- a force-push base, a shallow clone, a future workflow that resolves the range less carefully than ci.yml does -- gets 'ok' and exit 0 from both gates over a tree that violates them. The gate reports success having examined nothing, and the exit status carries that success downstream.

findings.title: The '~19 files' figure is measurably 31, and the grandfathering it describes is whitespace-fragile
findings.detail: MEASURED with the gate's own pattern and its own line filter over `git ls-files '*Test.java' '*Tests.java'`: 31 files, not ~19, and 48 matching lines (the review tree, which stages everything against an empty base, produces the same list). The figure appears twice -- the script header and the staged M0.77 row -- and it is what sizes M0.77. Separately, the grandfathering the same sentence relies on holds only for files nobody touches: MEASURED, re-indenting an already-committed inventory line by two spaces, with no change to its text, re-renders it as an added line and turns the gate red. Those 31 files are landmines for any future reformat or re-wrap. That may be the intended behaviour (fix the sentence you are touching), but it is not what 'grandfathered and will not fail CI' says. The other measured claims in the header check out exactly: archive median 1306, p90 5127, max 18845, and four of the top seven rows are M4.8-M4.9.
findings.mutation_that_survives: Not a mutation finding -- a false number and an overstated exemption in staged prose. The consequence is that whoever picks up M0.77 scopes it for 19 files and finds 31, or is surprised by a red gate on a pure reformat.
findings.remedy: Correct the count, and say that a legacy line is grandfathered only while untouched.
findings.failure_scenario: A session picks up M0.77 scoped for ~19 files, finds 31, and either overruns the task or sweeps a subset and closes the row -- leaving 12 files of the prose the row exists to remove. Separately, an unrelated reformat of any of those 31 files re-renders a legacy line as added and fails the commit on prose the author did not write, which the script header names as the way a gate gets turned off.
